metadata.case_name: TAM KAM FAI v. MICHAEL J DESIGN LTD AND OTHERS

source: “With Mr. Tam's moderate head injury, he should have recovered sufficiently by June 2003 (i.e. 1 year after the accident) to be able to resume gainful employment.”
"The combined residues from the stiffness of the right wrist, as well as the ulnar and median nerve injury would be compatible with a reasonable capacity in performing the daily activities."

"With respect to the orthopaedic injuries, he could work in selected light duty repair jobs... limited by the residual stiffness of the right wrist, as well as the weakness and residual numbness in the right hand."

manifestations.description: impaired motor power of right upper limb (under-performance on testing)
impaired motor power of left lower limb (under-performance on testing)
residual weakness in the right hand
residual numbness in the thumb and fingers
reduced capacity for fine work manoeuvres requiring repetitive use of fingers and thumb
reduced capacity for repeated heavy object lifting and continuous use of heavier tools
reduced capacity for prolonged walking and standing (left lower limb)
inability to return to pre-injury job handling heavy air conditioners

treatments_future: possible fusion operation of the right wrist

losses.description: Unable to return to pre-injury job handling heavy air conditioners; restricted to selected light duty jobs such as messenger/office assistant or building attendant/guard.
